title: Coffee: The World's Drug of Choice
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss coffee: a cold-open about the origin of the term "cup of joe" (cuppa tea, GI Joe slang), then the legend of Kaldi the Ethiopian goat herder, early African use of coffee berries, Arabica and Robusta, the Arabian Peninsula and Mecca export ban, Baba Budan's smuggling, Lieutenant Colonel Palheta's Brazil seedlings, the Dutch Java plantation, Pope Clement VIII's endorsement, coffeehouses (penny universities, Lloyd's of London, Boston Tea Party at the Green Dragon), coffee's economics, caffeine content, the coffee bean belt and growing, harvesting, wet and dry processing, grading, roasting, grinding and brewing tips, decaf methods, world coffee styles, health findings on diabetes, memory, bone density and weight, pesticides, fair trade, and a New Year sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and origin of 'cup of joe'
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about their coffee habits, then Josh explains that 'joe' comes from GI slang for coffee, linked to the British 'cuppa' and the American servicemen of World War Two.

segments.title: Legend of Kaldi and early coffee use
segments.summary: The legend of Kaldi the Ethiopian goat herder whose goats became frisky after eating red berries, and the prehistoric African use of coffee berries mixed with animal fat as energy bars.

segments.title: Coffee in Arabia and the coffeehouse tradition
segments.summary: Coffee roasting and brewing on the Arabian Peninsula, the Muslim export restrictions on beans and plants, the kaveh coffeehouses known as schools of the wise, and the penny universities of London.

segments.title: Spread of coffee to India, Java, and Brazil
segments.summary: Legends of Baba Budan smuggling beans out of Mecca to India, the first European coffee plantation in Java in 1616, and the Brazilian seedling story involving a Lieutenant Colonel sent to French Guiana.

segments.title: Pope Clement VIII and coffee in Europe
segments.summary: Europeans called coffee the devil's drink, and Pope Clement VIII tasted it and endorsed it, helping it become popular in Europe.

segments.title: Lloyd's of London, Boston Tea Party, and coffee in America
segments.summary: Lloyd's of London began in Edward Lloyd's coffeehouse, and the taxes on tea pushed Americans toward coffee, with the Boston Tea Party planned at the Green Dragon coffeehouse.

segments.title: Coffee economics and caffeine
segments.summary: Coffee is the second most traded commodity after petroleum and the most popular drink after water. Caffeine content of coffee compared with cola and other stimulants.

segments.title: Coffee plants, bean belt, and varieties
segments.summary: The bean belt between the tropics where coffee grows, Hawaii's Kona coffee, the coffee tree and cherry, and the Arabica and Robusta varieties with their growing requirements and flavor differences, including the Robusta blending history.

segments.title: Harvesting, processing, and drying coffee
segments.summary: Hand harvesting of ripe red cherries, the layers of the coffee cherry, harvest seasons north and south of the equator, dry and wet processing methods, and drying of green coffee.

segments.title: Roasting, grinding, and brewing
segments.summary: Grading green beans, roasting temperatures and stages including the pops, roastmasters cupping, nitrogen packaging, grind size for different brewing methods, and brewing ratios and water temperature.

segments.title: Closing discussion and sign-off
segments.summary: Discussion of health findings on coffee and diabetes, decaf processing, Starbucks, and a New Year greeting with contact information for the show.
